projects.name: Trinity Old Library / Long Room (TCD)
projects.what: Official Old Library page; links to library virtual tours and 3D floorplans.
projects.gap: Page only links 'Virtual Tours & 3D Floorplans'; Long Room-specific tour not confirmed; no reading, no map, no other libraries.
projects.lesson: Link out to official tours and credit the library; do not claim endorsement.

projects.name: Google Arts & Culture: 10 Incredible Libraries
projects.what: Editorial tour of 10 libraries (Trinity, Alexandrina, Marciana, NYPL, Clementinum...).
projects.overlap: Same famous-library set incl. Trinity Old Library.
projects.gap: Editorial photos only: no walkable replicas, no readable books, no lost libraries, no timeline.
projects.lesson: Good canonical list of libraries to cover.
projects.quote: Even if you're not a bookworm, you can't deny the magnificence of these 10 libraries around the world.

projects.name: Sketchfab 'library' models
projects.overlap: Source of CC 3D assets for library interiors.
projects.gap: Uncurated, inconsistent accuracy, no evidence tags, no reading, no map.
projects.lesson: Check per-model licence; mine for reference, do not rely on for accuracy.
projects.quote: Library 3D models ready to view and download for free.

projects.name: Assassin's Creed Origins Discovery Tour
projects.what: Combat-free educational mode with 75 guided tours of ancient Egypt (Wikipedia page fetched; Library of Alexandria content not confirmed there).
projects.overlap: Educational walkable ancient-world reconstruction with historian input.
projects.gap: Not library-specific (Alexandria library content unconfirmed); commercial game; no readable books; no evidence tags.
projects.lesson: Guided-tour layer with historian narration is proven for education.
projects.quote: Discovery Tour removes combat from the game entirely, allowing teachers to show this portion of the game to schoolchildren directly.

projects.name: Pergamon As It Once Was (VR + AI, ISPRS 2025)
projects.what: Academic VR reconstruction of ancient Pergamon with AI avatar guides.
projects.overlap: Lost-city reconstruction from archaeological data (abstract does not clearly name the library).
projects.gap: Abstract does not address uncertainty communication; no readable books; not a web app as far as fetched; no map/timeline.
projects.lesson: Our per-element evidence tags fill the gap academic VR leaves.
projects.quote: AI-driven characters function as narrative agents, guiding visitors through the virtual city and delivering interpretive content

projects.name: Wonderful Ephesus (Library of Celsus)
projects.what: App by Adam Nemeth: Ephesus and Library of Celsus reconstructed from laser scan.
projects.gap: Single site; app not web; no books; no evidence tags; no map.
projects.lesson: Scan-based ruins are the strongest evidence basis; tag it as such.
projects.quote: If you are not able to be at the real site in Ephesus, then you can feel and imagine that you are there.

projects.name: The Uncensored Library (Minecraft)
projects.what: RSF Minecraft server/map housing banned journalism as in-game books.
projects.overlap: Walk into a library and read books.
projects.gap: Single stylised building, Minecraft only, no accurate replicas, no map/timeline.
projects.lesson: Purpose and curation make it famous; strong narrative framing.
projects.quote: The texts within the library are contained in in-game book items, which can be opened and placed on stands to be read by multiple players at once.

projects.name: MyShelves
projects.what: three.js/r3f first-person library you fill from Open Library; carry, read, shelve books.
projects.overlap: Closest on interaction: walk, pick book, read, in browser.
projects.gap: Fictional user-built room; no real libraries, no lost libraries, no map, no manuscripts.
projects.lesson: Proves first-person take-book-read loop works in browser stack.
projects.quote: A 3D library you walk around in first person.

projects.name: 3D Bookshop
projects.what: Walk around virtual shop, pick up books and read via Foliate JS (EPUB/PDF/CBZ).
projects.overlap: Pick up book and read in-scene.
projects.gap: Bookshop not library; no historic replicas; no map.
projects.lesson: Foliate JS is a ready EPUB reader for Standard Ebooks files.
projects.quote: You can walk around, pick up books, flip them over to read the back cover, and open them to read a sample or the full book

projects.name: Library of Babel
projects.what: Borges-inspired site to browse, search, random-access generated texts.
projects.gap: No real texts, no 3D walk, no real libraries.
projects.lesson: Name/metaphor is crowded; avoid generic Babel branding.
projects.quote: By this art you may contemplate the variation of the 23 letters

projects.name: Internet Archive BookReader
projects.what: Open-source book viewer used across Internet Archive, embeddable.
projects.lesson: AGPL: reuse only if we accept copyleft; otherwise copy UX.
projects.quote: The Internet Archive BookReader is used to view books from the Internet Archive online and can also be used to view other books.

projects.name: Mirador
projects.gap: Flat viewer, no page-turn animation or 3D.
projects.lesson: Apache-2.0: safe to embed as the IIIF reading panel.
projects.quote: An open-source, web-based 'multi-up' viewer that supports zoom-pan-rotate functionality

projects.name: Universal Viewer
projects.what: Embeddable open-source viewer for images, documents, 3D via IIIF.
projects.lesson: Alternative IIIF viewer; check licence on GitHub before use.
projects.quote: Universal Viewer displays images, multimedia, documents and 3D models in an extensible and embeddable open-source application.

projects.name: StPageFlip
projects.lesson: MIT: usable; three.js bend-shader may look better inside a 3D scene.
projects.quote: Powerful, simple, and flexible JS Library for creating realistic and beautiful page turning effect.

projects.name: Turn.js
projects.quote: Turn.js is a plugin for jQuery that adds a beautiful transition similar to real pages in a book or magazine.

projects.name: World Digital Library
projects.what: Library of Congress/UNESCO digital library; retired 2020-21, wdl.org now redirects to a static LoC page.
projects.overlap: Global heritage texts with browse by place and time (map/timeline not confirmed on this page).
projects.lesson: Cautionary: institutional projects get retired; keep our data exportable.
projects.quote: make available on the Internet, free of charge and in multilingual format, significant primary materials from cultures

projects.name: Wikidata WikiProject Libraries
projects.what: 155,412 library items in Wikidata with ontology and SPARQL queries.
projects.overlap: Source for coordinates/metadata of existing libraries.
projects.gap: Data only; no map UI shown, no lost-library reconstructions.
projects.quote: define a structure for libraries and to create and improve the items about library

closest: Pergamon As It Once Was (VR + AI, ISPRS 2025)
verdict: No fetched project combines accurate replicas, evidence-tagged lost-library reconstructions, readable public-domain books and a map/timeline. Pieces exist separately: walk-and-read 3D (MyShelves, 3D Bookshop), academic VR of lost sites (Pergamon, Celsus), flat viewers (Mirador, BookReader). Search was limited (about 35 calls), so absence is not proven; Alexandria, Nalanda and Nineveh reconstructions were not found.
